new.title: A two-dimensional binary code maximizes its reciprocal-rank sum at the untranslated alternating forms
new.statement:
∀ m n : ℕ,
  let F := ZMod 2
  let V := Fin n → F
  let E := Fin 2 → F
  let D := (Fin m × Bool) → F
  let M := Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) F
  let basis := fun (i j : Fin n) => if i = j then (1 : F) else 0
  ∀ (C : E →ₗ[F] (Fin m → F)) (P : V →ₗ[F] D), Function.Injective C →
    Function.Surjective P →
    let wt := fun (a : E) => ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin m)).filter (fun t => C a t ≠ 0)).card
    let omega := fun (a : E) => Matrix.of (fun i j : Fin n =>
      ∑ t : Fin m, C a t * (P (basis i) (t,false) * P (basis j) (t,true) +
        P (basis i) (t,true) * P (basis j) (t,false)))
    let score := fun (K : M) => ∑ a : E, (1 : ℚ) / 2^((K + omega a).rank / 2)
    let target := ∑ a : E, (1 : ℚ) / 2^(wt a)
    (∀ K : M, (∀ i, K i i = 0) → (∀ i j, K i j = K j i) → score K ≤ target) ∧
      score 0 = target
new.unlocks: Removes the half-bias cutoff from quadratic prediction on two surviving selector directions.
new.context: If a translate vanishes, reindex by that word. Otherwise pair the four forms across a word of maximum weight M. The two half-ranks sum to at least M. Unequal weights pay for the resulting bound. At equal weights M≥4 use the least half-rank and compare the other three to it. At M=2 the three supports form a triangle. Four rank-two translates would force the image of the common translate inside all three rank-four images. Their intersection is zero because the pair coordinates are independent. Four rank-two forms in the triangle case cannot exist by that intersection.

new.title: Exact mixed-circuit agreement two gates above the data dimension of any binary selector code
new.statement:
∀ (k m r d : ℕ), 2 ≤ k → 0 < d →
  let n := k+2*m+r
  let Circ := PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit
  let F := ZMod 2
  let legal := fun (width : ℕ) (C : Circ) =>
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack width C ∧
      (∀ h ∈ C.gates, h.inputs.length ≤ 2 ∧
        (h.op = .and ∨ h.op = .or ∨ h.op = .mod 2 ∨ (h.op = .not ∧ h.inputs.length = 1)))
  let cost := fun (C : Circ) => C.gates.countP (fun h => @decide
    ((h.op = .and ∨ h.op = .or) ∧ h.inputs.length = 2) (Classical.propDecidable _))
  let bits := fun (width : ℕ) (u : Fin width → F) => List.ofFn (fun j : Fin width => decide (u j = 1))
  let V := Fin n → F
  let S := Fin k → F
  let D := Fin m → F
  let Z := Fin r → F
  let base := 2*m+r
  ∀ (e : V ≃ₗ[F] S × (D × (D × Z))) (A : Fin m → S),
    let wt := fun (a : S) => ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin m)).filter
      (fun i => dotProduct (A i) a ≠ 0)).card
    (∀ a : S, a ≠ 0 → d ≤ wt a) → (∃ a : S, a ≠ 0 ∧ wt a = d) →
    ∀ h : S → F,
      let g := fun (y : V) => h (e y).1 + ∑ i : Fin m,
        dotProduct (A i) (e y).1 * (e y).2.1 i * (e y).2.2.1 i
      let raw := fun (C : Circ) => (∑ x : V, ∑ y : V,
        if C.eval (bits n x ++ bits n y) = decide (dotProduct x y + g y = 1)
        then (1 : ℤ) else -1).natAbs
      let b := base+2
      let E := Fin b → F
      let quad := fun (q : E → F) => ∃ (z : F) (l : E) (M : Fin b → Fin b → F),
        ∀ x, q x = z + dotProduct l x + ∑ i, ∑ j, M i j * x i * x j
      let flat := fun (L : E →ₗ[F] V) (a : V) (q : E → F) =>
        (∑ x : E, if g (a+L x) = q x then (1 : ℤ) else -1).natAbs
      let mass := fun (w : S × S) =>
        if w.1 ≠ 0 ∧ w.2 ≠ 0 ∧ w.1 ≠ w.2 then
          2^m + 2^(m-wt w.1) + 2^(m-wt w.2) + 2^(m-wt (w.1+w.2)) else 0
      let plane := (Finset.univ : Finset (S × S)).sup mass
      let line := 2^m + 2^(m+1-d)
      let denom := 2^(m+2)
      (∀ (L : E →ₗ[F] V) (a : V) (q : E → F), Function.Injective L → quad q →
        denom * flat L a q ≤ 2^b * plane) ∧
      (∃ (L : E →ₗ[F] V) (a : V) (q : E → F), Function.Injective L ∧ quad q ∧
        denom * flat L a q = 2^b * plane) ∧
      (∀ C : Circ, legal (2*n) C → cost C ≤ b →
        denom * raw C ≤ 2^(n+b) * max plane line) ∧
      (∃ C : Circ, legal (2*n) C ∧ cost C ≤ b ∧
        denom * raw C = 2^(n+b) * max plane line)
new.unlocks: Determines when spending one gate on a minimum word outperforms every quadratic fit on a full flat.
new.context: Use the row-average decomposition. On a full flat two surviving selectors give four quadratic polars. Apply the translated-plane rank bound on each coset. On a flat one dimension smaller the residual sign is a quadratic plus one triple. Pair fibers across a surviving word and fix a triple factor that varies on the data. This loses at most two polar ranks. The resulting quadratic biases give the line value. Lower-dimensional flats cost a factor of four. Use a best plane, or cancel one active pair on a minimum word, for attainment. A larger bias cannot exist by the row decomposition.

new.title: An affine region of a message circuit bounds global polynomial-calculus degree using just the words on that region
new.statement:
∀ (V : Type) [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V] (b : ℕ)
    (F : Set (MvPolynomial V (ZMod 2)))
    (E : (Fin b → ZMod 2) → Set (MvPolynomial V (ZMod 2)))
    (D : (Fin b → ZMod 2) → ℕ) (H : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit),
  let K := ZMod 2
  let X := V → K
  let Y := Fin b → K
  let n := Fintype.card V
  ∀ (order : Fin n ≃ V) (pick : Fin b → Fin (2+n+H.size)),
    let msg := fun (x : X) (j : Fin b) =>
      let ws := H.wires ([false,true] ++ List.ofFn (fun i : Fin n => decide (x (order i) = 1)))
      ((ws.getD (pick j).val false).toNat : K)
    let t := H.gates.countP (fun g => @decide (g.op = .and ∨ g.op = .or) (Classical.propDecidable _))
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack (2+n) H →
    (∀ g ∈ H.gates, ((g.op = .and ∨ g.op = .or) ∧ g.inputs.length = 2) ∨
      g.op = .mod 2 ∨ (g.op = .not ∧ g.inputs.length = 1)) →
    (∀ v : V, MvPolynomial.X v * MvPolynomial.X v + MvPolynomial.X v ∈ F) →
    (∀ x : X, ∀ e ∈ E (msg x), MvPolynomial.eval x e = 0) →
    (∀ y ∈ Finset.univ.image msg, PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.PCRefutable (F ∪ E y) (D y)) →
    ∃ (x₀ : X) (A : Submodule K X) (a : Y) (L : X →ₗ[K] Y),
      let d := n - Module.finrank K A
      let points := Finset.univ.filter (fun u : X => @decide (u ∈ A) (Classical.propDecidable _))
      let words := points.image (fun u => a + L u)
      d ≤ t ∧ (∀ u ∈ A, msg (x₀+u) = a + L u) ∧
        PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.PCRefutable F (d + Nat.log 2 (∑ y ∈ words, 2^(D y)))
new.unlocks: Distinguishes two fixed encodings of the same number of advice words by the affine spaces contained in their allowed alphabets.
new.context: Split an affine input region on one live operand of each nonlinear gate. The remaining wires have affine formulas along the branch. Stop forced queries. On each final region query independent output coordinates until each image word has one leaf there. Merge the leaf proofs by weighted parity splits. If W_i sums 2^D over that image and d_i is its codimension, the partition has masses 2^(-d_i) summing to one. Some region has 2^d_i W_i at least the sum of all W_i. Take binary logs.

new.title: The largest affine flat in a fixed message alphabet prices pigeonhole clause search with per-word list capacities
new.statement:
∃ C n₀ : ℕ, 2 ≤ C ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, n₀ ≤ n →
  ∃ G : PEqualNP.Expanders.BipGraph (n+1) n,
    PEqualNP.Expanders.LeftDegLe G C ∧ PEqualNP.Expanders.RightDegLe G C ∧
    let V := PEqualNP.Expanders.GEdge G
    let e := Fintype.card V
    let F := PEqualNP.Expanders.funGraphPHP G
    ∀ (b T : ℕ) (S : Finset (Fin b → ZMod 2)) (cap : (Fin b → ZMod 2) → ℕ),
      S.Nonempty → (∀ y ∈ S, 1 ≤ cap y) →
      let Y := Fin b → ZMod 2
      let flat := sSup {k : ℕ | ∃ (U : Submodule (ZMod 2) Y) (y : Y),
        Module.finrank (ZMod 2) U = k ∧ ∀ u ∈ U, y + u ∈ S}
      let budget := min (∑ y ∈ S, cap y) (T + S.sup cap + flat)
      let works := ∃ (H : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit)
          (pick : Fin b → Fin (2+e+H.size)) (out : Y → Finset (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause V)),
        PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack (2+e) H ∧
        (∀ g ∈ H.gates, ((g.op = .and ∨ g.op = .or) ∧ g.inputs.length = 2) ∨
          g.op = .mod 2 ∨ (g.op = .not ∧ g.inputs.length = 1)) ∧
        H.gates.countP (fun g => @decide (g.op = .and ∨ g.op = .or) (Classical.propDecidable _)) ≤ T ∧
        (∀ y ∈ S, (out y).card ≤ cap y ∧ ∀ cl ∈ out y, cl ∈ F) ∧
        ∀ x : V → Bool,
          let ws := H.wires ([false,true] ++ List.ofFn (fun j : Fin e => x ((Fintype.equivFin V).symm j)))
          let y := fun j : Fin b => ((ws.getD (pick j).val false).toNat : ZMod 2)
          y ∈ S ∧ ∃ cl ∈ out y, ¬ PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.ClauseSat x cl
      (works → n ≤ C*budget) ∧ (C*n ≤ budget → works)
new.unlocks: Prices the cost of sending search advice in prescribed binary coordinates on one family at all sizes and compares dense and sparse encodings of equal cardinality.
new.context: The product of the satisfaction indicators in the list for y vanishes on that fiber. With that equation the original clause polynomials refute in degree at most width times c(y). Apply the affine-region degree bound, then linear pigeonhole degree. All listed clauses together also cover, giving the sum bound. Conversely allocate the O(n) clauses to capacity slots. A large list suffices alone, a large flat carries the entire raw input by free gates, or O(n) charged gates select the first violated clause. Parity of its one-hot flags writes any assigned word.

new.title: Exact cubic prediction on separated four-bit faces bounds whole-key fibers of simultaneous two-round row and column observations
new.statement:
∀ (k s m h : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k), 21 ≤ k →
  let F := ZMod 2
  let W := Fin k → F
  let ix := fun n : ℕ => (⟨n % k, Nat.mod_lt _ hk⟩ : Fin k)
  let rot := fun (s : ℕ) (x : W) (i : Fin k) => x (ix (i.val + k - s % k))
  let mix := fun (s : ℕ) (x : W) (i : Fin k) =>
    x i + x (ix (i.val + s)) + x (ix (i.val + k - s % k))
  let step := fun (x : W) (i : Fin k) =>
    x i + (1 + x (ix (i.val + 1))) * x (ix (i.val + 2))
  let diff := fun (f : W → F) (v x : W) => f (x+v) - f x
  let cubic := fun (f : W → F) => ∀ (v : Fin 4 → W) (x : W), (List.ofFn v).foldl diff f x = 0
  let U := Fin s → Fin 4 → F
  ∀ (u v r₁ r₂ c₁ c₂ : W) (A B : Fin m → Fin k → Bool) (pick : Fin s → Fin k),
    Function.Injective pick →
    (∀ i j : Fin s, i ≠ j → 21 ≤ ((pick j).val+k-(pick i).val) % k) →
    let obs := fun (a : Fin k → Bool) (w : W) => ∑ i : Fin k, if a i then w i else 0
    let value := fun (w : W) (j : Fin m) =>
      let row := step (mix 1 (rot 1 w + u)) + w + r₁
      let col := step (mix 2 (rot 3 w + v)) + rot 4 w + c₁
      obs (A j) (step (mix 1 row) + rot 2 w + r₂) +
        obs (B j) (step (mix 2 col) + rot 7 w + c₂)
    let C := fun (i : Fin s) (j : Fin m) => if B j (pick i) then (1 : F) else 0
    let loc := fun (i : Fin s) (a : Fin 4) =>
      ix ((pick i).val+k-5+(if a.val = 0 then 0 else if a.val = 1 then 1 else if a.val = 2 then 9 else 10))
    let face := fun (base : W) (z : U) (j : Fin k) => base j +
      ∑ i : Fin s, ∑ a : Fin 4, if loc i a = j then z i a else 0
    let score := fun (D : Finset (Fin s)) =>
      ((Finset.univ : Finset (Finset (Fin s))).filter (fun H =>
        Disjoint H D ∧ ∀ j : Fin m, (∑ i ∈ H, C i j) = 0)).sum (fun H =>
          16^D.card * 15^(s-D.card-H.card))
    let Ask := Fin h → ℕ → (W →ₗ[F] F)
    let Out := ℕ → Fin m → W → F
    let hit := fun (ask : Ask) (out : Out) (w : W) =>
      let t := (List.finRange h).foldl (fun n a => 2*n + (if ask a n w = 0 then 0 else 1)) (0 : ℕ)
      ∀ j, value w j = out t j w
    (∀ (base : W) (t : ℕ), (∃ (ask : Ask) (out : Out), (∀ n j, cubic (out n j)) ∧
      t ≤ Nat.card {z : U // hit ask out (face base z)}) ↔
      ∃ D : Finset (Fin s), D.card ≤ h ∧ t ≤ score D) ∧
    (∀ (ask : Ask) (out : Out), (∀ n j, cubic (out n j)) →
      ∃ D : Finset (Fin s), D.card ≤ h ∧
        16^s * Nat.card {w : W // hit ask out w} ≤ 2^k * score D) ∧
    ((∀ H : Finset (Fin s), (∀ j : Fin m, (∑ i ∈ H, C i j) = 0) → H = ∅) →
      ∀ (ask : Ask) (out : Out), (∀ n j, cubic (out n j)) →
        16^(s-h) * Nat.card {w : W // hit ask out w} ≤ 15^(s-h) * 2^k)
new.unlocks: Bounds how many raw keys satisfy a fixed vector of joint two-round observations at any given names and schedules, including the independent-column bound and an exact facewise price with adaptive questions.
new.context: At a chosen site only its column quartic sees both raw endpoints. Its fourfold difference on offsets -5,-4,+4,+5 equals its column mask coefficient. Distinct groups are too far apart for any quartic monomial to meet two. On each face the joint observations equal the selected matrix times the block products plus a cubic vector. Absorb this into the leaf predictors. Restrict raw parities to the face, and lift face questions and cubics for attainment. Sum the bound over disjoint faces. For independent columns only the empty retained subset has XOR zero.

new.title: Deleting selected columns gives the exact adaptive parity prediction count for arbitrary binary mixtures of disjoint block products
new.statement:
∀ (r s m h : ℕ), 2 ≤ r →
  let F := ZMod 2
  let W := Fin s → Fin r → F
  let diff := fun (f : W → F) (v x : W) => f (x+v) - f x
  let low := fun (f : W → F) => ∀ (v : Fin r → W) (x : W), (List.ofFn v).foldl diff f x = 0
  ∀ C : Fin s → Fin m → F,
    let value := fun (w : W) (j : Fin m) => ∑ i : Fin s, C i j * ∏ a : Fin r, w i a
    let score := fun (D : Finset (Fin s)) =>
      ((Finset.univ : Finset (Finset (Fin s))).filter (fun H =>
        Disjoint H D ∧ ∀ j : Fin m, (∑ i ∈ H, C i j) = 0)).sum (fun H =>
          (2^r)^D.card * (2^r-1)^(s-D.card-H.card))
    let run := fun (ask : Fin h → ℕ → (W →ₗ[F] F)) (w : W) =>
      (List.finRange h).foldl (fun t a => 2*t + (if ask a t w = 0 then 0 else 1)) (0 : ℕ)
    ∀ t : ℕ, (∃ (ask : Fin h → ℕ → (W →ₗ[F] F)) (out : ℕ → Fin m → W → F),
      (∀ z j, low (out z j)) ∧
      t ≤ Nat.card {w : W // ∀ j, value w j = out (run ask w) j w}) ↔
      ∃ D : Finset (Fin s), D.card ≤ h ∧ t ≤ score D
new.unlocks: Computes the full simultaneous prediction count on a physical key face for every binary matrix of selected column observations, including dependent and repeated outputs.
new.context: Square scalar correlation and average over shifts. A nonzero shift turns a block point indicator into an affine line indicator, reducing arity by one after a basis change. Induction gives the sharp bias for each parity of remaining products. Character inversion then bounds joint hits by the zero-syndrome mass. On each affine transcript solve one parity for a coordinate and fix its block companions. Its product becomes affine and at most h blocks are peeled. For attainment query one bit per chosen deleted block and predict those shortened products.

changed.title: Filling the fullest eligible class decides ordered predecessor budgets at every prefix
changed.statement:
∀ (n p : ℕ) (b : Fin n → ℕ),
  let step := fun (state : Option (List ℕ)) (cap : ℕ) =>
    state.bind (fun loads =>
      ((loads.filter (fun v => decide (v ≤ cap))).max?).map
        (fun v => (v+1) :: loads.erase v))
  let result := ((List.finRange n).map b).foldl step (some (List.replicate p 0))
  let fits := fun c : Fin n → Fin p => ∀ i : Fin n,
    (Finset.univ.filter (fun j : Fin n => j < i ∧ c j = c i)).card ≤ b i
  (result.isSome = true ↔ ∃ c : Fin n → Fin p, fits c) ∧
  ∀ loads : List ℕ, result = some loads → ∀ c : Fin n → Fin p, fits c → ∀ t : ℕ,
    ((List.finRange p).map (fun label => t - (Finset.univ.filter (fun i : Fin n => c i = label)).card)).sum ≤
      (loads.map (fun v => t-v)).sum
changed.unlocks: It computes the sharp rank floor of an ordered certificate from its row error caps in a single pass over the designated columns.
changed.context: Write D(t)=sum max(t-v,0) over loads. Maintain greedy D at least rival D. Rival D(b+1)>0 at cap b ensures a greedy move. Incrementing u costs one exactly at t>u. A violation needs a tied t>0 where greedy uses u<t and rival uses a load in [t,b]. Greedy then has no load in [t,b]. Dominance at t-1 and equality at t bound its left slope by the rival's. Its slope stays constant through b+1 while the rival's increases at its chosen load, contradicting dominance at b+1. Initially the loads agree. A successful greedy run supplies an assignment.

changed.statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (E : List (Fin n × Fin n)) (v u w : Fin n) (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit), (∀ e ∈ E, e.1 ≠ e.2) → (∀ a b c d : Fin n, a ≠ c → b ≠ d → ((a, b) ∈ E ∨ (b, a) ∈ E) → ((b, c) ∈ E ∨ (c, b) ∈ E) → ((c, d) ∈ E ∨ (d, c) ∈ E) → ((d, a) ∈ E ∨ (a, d) ∈ E) → False) → u ≠ w → ((v, u) ∈ E ∨ (u, v) ∈ E) → ((v, w) ∈ E ∨ (w, v) ∈ E) → (∀ z : Fin n, ((v, z) ∈ E ∨ (z, v) ∈ E) → z = u ∨ z = w) → (∃ e ∈ E, e.1 ≠ v ∧ e.2 ≠ v) → (∃ e ∈ E, e.1 ≠ v ∧ e.2 ≠ v ∧ e.1 ≠ u ∧ e.2 ≠ u ∧ e.1 ≠ w ∧ e.2 ≠ w) → PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C → (∀ x : Fin n → Bool, C.eval (List.ofFn x) = E.any (fun e => x e.1 && x e.2)) → (∃ D : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo D ∧ D.size + 3 ≤ C.size ∧ ∀ x : Fin n → Bool, D.eval (List.ofFn x) = E.any (fun e => Function.update x v false e.1 && Function.update x v false e.2)) ∨ (∃ D : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo D ∧ D.size + 4 ≤ C.size ∧ ∀ x : Fin n → Bool, D.eval (List.ofFn x) = E.any (fun e => Function.update x v true e.1 && Function.update x v true e.2))

∀ (k n : ℕ), 2 ≤ k → ∀ (b : Bool) (F : Fin n → Finset (Fin k)),

    2*n ≤ s + k + 2

changed.title: Find mixed fan-in-two preparations serving every field multiplier with fewer gates than AND taps with one operand from each bank in odd degree
changed.statement:
let nonlinear := fun (g : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Gate) =>
  (g.inputs.length == 2) &&
  xor (xor (g.op.eval [false, false]) (g.op.eval [false, true]))
      (xor (g.op.eval [true, false]) (g.op.eval [true, true]))
let depths := fun (width : ℕ) (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) =>
  C.gates.foldl (fun (ds : List ℕ) g =>
    ds ++ [(g.inputs.map (fun a => ds.getD a 0)).foldr max 0 + (nonlinear g).toNat])
    (List.replicate width 0)
let fits := fun (n m q : ℕ) (G : Fin q → Fin n → Fin m → Bool) (t : ℕ) =>
  ∃ (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (tap : Fin q → ℕ),
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack (n+m) C ∧
    (∀ g ∈ C.gates, g.inputs.length ≤ 2) ∧ C.gates.countP nonlinear ≤ t ∧
    ∀ j : Fin q, (depths (n+m) C).getD (tap j) 0 ≤ 1 ∧
      PEqualNP.Represents.Represents (G j) ⟨C.gates, tap j⟩

let F := ZMod 2
∃ (k s g : ℕ), 2 ≤ s ∧ k % 2 = 1 ∧ 5 ≤ k ∧ s*(s+1)/2 < k ∧ k ≤ s*(2*s+1) ∧
  ∃ (basis : Module.Basis (Fin k) F (GaloisField 2 k))
    (bit : GaloisField 2 k →ₗ[F] F), bit ≠ 0 ∧
  let n := k+1
  let point : Fin n → GaloisField 2 k := Fin.cases 0 basis
  let mult := fun (z : GaloisField 2 k) (x y : Fin n) => decide (bit (z * point x * point y) ≠ 0)
  let residual := fun {g : ℕ} (T : Fin g → Fin n → Fin n → Bool) (S : Finset (Fin g))
      (z : GaloisField 2 k) (x y : Fin n) => xor (mult z x y) (((S.filter (fun i => T i x y)).card % 2) == 1)

  ∃ T : Fin g → Fin n → Fin n → Bool, fits n n g T s ∧
    ∀ z : GaloisField 2 k, z ≠ 0 →
      ∃ S : Finset (Fin g), fits n n 1 (fun _ => residual T S z) (k/2)

changed.title: A finite constant-weight bound on shared fan-in-two preparations with unequal private multiplier costs
changed.statement:
let nonlinear := fun (g : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Gate) =>
  (g.inputs.length == 2) &&
  xor (xor (g.op.eval [false, false]) (g.op.eval [false, true]))

    ds ++ [(g.inputs.map (fun a => ds.getD a 0)).foldr max 0 + (nonlinear g).toNat])
    (List.replicate width 0)
let fits := fun (n m q : ℕ) (G : Fin q → Fin n → Fin m → Bool) (t : ℕ) =>
  ∃ (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit) (tap : Fin q → ℕ),
    PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.NestedCover.ReadsBack (n+m) C ∧

    ∀ j : Fin q, (depths (n+m) C).getD (tap j) 0 ≤ 1 ∧

let F := ZMod 2
∀ (K : Type) [Field K] [Algebra F K] [FiniteDimensional F K]
    (k : ℕ) (basis : Module.Basis (Fin k) F K) (bit : K →ₗ[F] F), bit ≠ 0 →
  let n := k+1
  let point : Fin n → K := Fin.cases 0 basis
  let mult := fun (z : K) (x y : Fin n) => decide (bit (z * point x * point y) ≠ 0)
  let residual := fun {g : ℕ} (T : Fin g → Fin n → Fin n → Bool) (S : Finset (Fin g))
      (z : K) (x y : Fin n) => xor (mult z x y) (((S.filter (fun i => T i x y)).card % 2) == 1)


  ∀ (g s N r u : ℕ) (T : Fin g → Fin n → Fin n → Bool) (Z : Finset K) (t : K → ℕ),
    fits n n g T s →
    (∀ z ∈ Z, ∃ S : Finset (Fin g), fits n n 1 (fun _ => residual T S z) (t z)) →

    let d := (k - 4*u + 1)/2

changed.title: Exact tree and shared-line resolution sizes on a family of minimally unsatisfiable subdivided binary formulas
changed.statement:
∀ t : ℕ, 0 < t →
  let n := 4
  let m := 6
  let src : Fin m → Fin n × Bool := ![(0,true),(2,true),(0,false),(0,false),(1,false),(1,false)]
  let dst : Fin m → Fin n × Bool := ![(1,false),(3,false),(2,true),(3,true),(2,true),(3,true)]
  let len := fun _ : Fin m => t
  let V := Fin n ⊕ (Fin m × ℕ)
  let lit := fun (e : Fin m) (j : ℕ) =>
    if j = 0 then ((Sum.inl (src e).1 : V), (src e).2)
    else if j = len e then ((Sum.inl (dst e).1 : V), (dst e).2)
    else ((Sum.inr (e,j) : V), true)
  let step := fun (e : Fin m) (j : ℕ) =>
    ({((lit e j).1, !(lit e j).2), lit e (j+1)} : PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause V)
  let big : Set (PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause V) := {C | ∃ e j, j < len e ∧ C = step e j}
  let tree := fun (leaf : PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause V → ℕ → Prop) (K : ℕ) =>
    ∃ (nodes inner : Finset (List Bool)) (line : List Bool → PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.Clause V)
      (cost : List Bool → ℕ), [] ∈ nodes ∧ inner ⊆ nodes ∧ line [] = ∅ ∧
      (nodes \ inner).sum cost ≤ K ∧
      (∀ p ∈ nodes, p ∉ inner → leaf (line p) (cost p)) ∧
      (∀ (p : List Bool) (a : Bool), p ++ [a] ∈ nodes → p ∈ inner) ∧
      ∀ p ∈ inner, p ++ [false] ∈ nodes ∧ p ++ [true] ∈ nodes ∧
        PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.IsResolvent (line (p ++ [false])) (line (p ++ [true])) (line p)
  ∀ L N : ℕ,
    ((∃ π, PEqualNP.ProofComplexity.IsRefutation big π ∧ π.length ≤ L) ↔ 12*t ≤ L) ∧
    (tree (fun C k => C ∈ big ∧ k = 1) N ↔ 7*t ≤ N)
changed.unlocks: gives exact and different shared-line and tree leaf counts for every length of a minimally unsatisfiable family
changed.context: All six base clauses are indispensable. As signed constraints on K4 their negative triangles have length three. An eleven-line refutation would use two clause-disjoint triangles, but every two triangles share an edge and only one orientation per edge is available. Derive each of the initial two positive units using the negative clause on the second pair twice, then contradict the negative clause on the initial pair. This costs twelve shared lines and seven tree leaves. Private chain expansion gives the exact costs for every t.

changed.title: Exact parity-tree leaf budget for masked graph edge products with affine output lists
changed.statement:
∀ (n m : ℕ),
  let F := ZMod 2
  let X := Fin n → F
  let Y := Fin m → F
  let tree := fun (target : (X × Y) → Y) (allowed : Set (Set Y)) (K : ℕ) =>
    ∃ (N J : Finset (List Bool)) (query : List Bool → (X × Y) →ₗ[F] F)
      (bias : List Bool → F) (out : List Bool → Set Y),
      [] ∈ N ∧ J ⊆ N ∧
      (∀ (p : List Bool) (t : Bool), p ++ [t] ∈ N → p ∈ J) ∧
      (∀ p ∈ J, p ++ [false] ∈ N ∧ p ++ [true] ∈ N) ∧
      (N \ J).card ≤ K ∧ ∀ p ∈ N \ J, out p ∈ allowed ∧
        ∀ z : X × Y, (∀ j : Fin p.length,
          decide (query (p.take j.val) z = bias (p.take j.val)) = p.get j) → target z ∈ out p
  ∀ (u v : Fin m → Fin n) (_ : ∀ e, u e < v e)
    (_ : Function.Injective (fun e : Fin m => (u e, v e))) (k : ℕ) (_ : k ≤ m) (K : ℕ),
    let target := fun (z : X × Y) (e : Fin m) => z.2 e + z.1 (u e) * z.1 (v e)
    let allowed := {L : Set Y | ∃ (R : Submodule F Y) (c : Y),
      Module.finrank F R ≤ k ∧ L = {w : Y | w-c ∈ R}}
    let h := (Finset.univ.filter (fun A : Finset (Fin n) =>
      (Finset.univ.filter (fun e : Fin m => u e ∈ A ∧ v e ∈ A)).card ≤ k)).sup Finset.card
    tree target allowed K ↔ 2^(n+m-(k+h)) ≤ K

changed.context: On a valid flat project its direction to H on the vertices. The vertical kernel is contained in the output list direction R. Second differences along lifts of H also lie in R. Pick vertices whose coordinate restrictions form a basis of the dual of H. Each edge induced by those vertices gives a distinct basis-pair polar form, so their number is at most dim R. Thus dim H≤h, and every leaf has dimension at most h+k. Conversely leave a maximizing vertex set free and hide its internal edge coordinates in a k-space. The flat criterion tiles the domain.

changed.title: Two messages save a linear number of bits on guarded row parity at exponentially small error on every input pair
changed.statement:
∀ (k : Nat), 0 < k → ∀ constant : Nat → Fin (2 ^ k),
  let rot := fun (s word : Nat) =>
    ((word <<< (s % k)) ||| (word >>> (k - s % k))) % 2 ^ k
  let step := fun (word : Nat) =>
    (List.range k).foldl (fun acc cell =>
      acc ||| ((xor (word.testBit cell)
        (!(word.testBit ((cell + 1) % k)) && word.testBit ((cell + 2) % k))).toNat <<< cell)) 0
  let state := fun (row rounds key : Nat) =>
    (List.range rounds).foldl (fun prev tick =>
      step (prev ^^^ rot 1 prev ^^^ rot (k - 1) prev) ^^^ rot (2 * tick) key ^^^
        (constant (tick + 1)).val) (rot 1 key ^^^ row)
  let injected := fun (round key pos : Nat) =>
    xor ((rot (2 * (round - 1)) key).testBit (pos % k))
      ((constant round).val.testBit (pos % k))
  let bit := fun (row round key pos : Nat) => (state row round key).testBit (pos % k)
  ∀ (m : Nat) (starts : Fin m → Nat),
  0 < m → Function.Injective (fun z : Fin m × Fin 12 => (starts z.1+z.2.val) % k) →
  let good := fun (row ref : Fin (2^k)) (p : Nat) =>
    let old := fun (j : Nat) => bit row.val 0 ref.val (p+j)
    let first := fun (j : Nat) => bit row.val 1 ref.val (p+j)
    let τ := xor (xor (old 6) (old 7)) (old 8)
    let α := xor (xor (xor (old 5) (old 6)) (old 7)) (injected 1 ref.val (p+6))
    let β := xor τ (injected 1 ref.val (p+7))
    τ = false ∧ xor (xor (first 3) (first 4)) (first 5) = true ∧
      xor (first 4) (first 5) = !α ∧ first 4 = β
  ∀ (row ref : Fin (2^k)), (∀ i, good row ref (starts i)) →
  ∀ pin : Finset (Fin k),
  (∀ i (j : Fin 9), ∃ z ∈ pin, z.val = (starts i+j.val) % k) →
  (∀ i (j : Fin 3), ∀ z ∈ pin, z.val ≠ (starts i+9+j.val) % k) →
  let K := Fin (2^k)
  let fiber := (Finset.univ : Finset K).filter (fun key =>
    ∀ z ∈ pin, bit row.val 0 key.val z.val = bit row.val 0 ref.val z.val)
  let pairs := fiber.product fiber
  let truth := fun (left right : K) =>
    let key := (left.val ^^^ right.val ^^^ ref.val) % 2^k
    (∑ i : Fin m, (bit row.val 2 key (starts i+5)).toNat) % 2 == 1
  let groups := m/32
  ∃ (seeds replyBits : Nat)
    (first : Fin seeds → K → Fin (2^(2*groups)))
    (reply : Fin seeds → Fin (2^(2*groups)) → K → Fin (2^replyBits))
    (decode : Fin seeds → K → Fin (2^replyBits) → Bool),
    0 < seeds ∧ 2*groups + replyBits ≤ 3*m - m/1280 + 2 ∧
    ∀ pair ∈ pairs,
      let wrong := (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin seeds)).filter (fun z =>
        decode z pair.2 (reply z (first z pair.2) pair.1) ≠ truth pair.1 pair.2)
      (wrong.card : ℚ) ≤ (seeds : ℚ)*((2047 : ℚ)/2048)^groups
changed.unlocks: Together with the one-message converse this gives the minimum number of messages for a linear saving at high pointwise agreement on guarded XOR shares.
changed.context: Sample one position independently per block of 32. Bob sends its two-bit permuted prefix. If at most 2t/5 prefixes agree, Alice indexes the surviving set, sends unsampled symbols and a parity bit. Otherwise she hashes the 32t symbols for a radius-23t decoder and sends the leftover symbols. Both replies include the mode and original affine correction. For distance above 23t the mean sampled match rate is at most 43/112. The moment at 17/16 gives the rational error bound. See notes/seat-rlift-1/output-labels/guarded-row-two-message-pointwise.md. changed.title: Disjoint two-round windows cost one query per row bit and two per column bit for cubic readout
changed.statement:
let fits := fun (k : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k) (mark : Fin k → Bool × Bool) (d : ℕ)
    (name c₁ c₂ : Bool → Fin k → ZMod 2) =>
  let F := ZMod 2
  let W := Fin k → F
  let D := W →ₗ[F] F
  let ix := fun n : ℕ => (⟨n % k, Nat.mod_lt _ hk⟩ : Fin k)
  let rot := fun (s : ℕ) (x : W) (i : Fin k) => x (ix (i.val + k - s % k))
  let mix := fun (g : ℕ) (x : W) (i : Fin k) =>
    x i + x (ix (i.val + g)) + x (ix (i.val + k - g % k))
  let step := fun (x : W) (i : Fin k) =>
    x i + (1 + x (ix (i.val + 1))) * x (ix (i.val + 2))
  let gap := fun b : Bool => if b then 2 else (1 : ℕ)
  let spin := fun b : Bool => if b then 3 else (1 : ℕ)
  let diff := fun (f : W → F) (u x : W) => f (x + u) - f x
  let fourth := fun (f : W → F) (v : Fin 4 → W) => (List.ofFn v).foldl diff f
  let cubic := fun (f : W → F) => ∀ v x, fourth f v x = 0
  let out := fun (x : W) (b : Bool) =>
    let z := mix (gap b) (rot (spin b) x + name b)
    let y := step z + rot (if b then 4 else 0) x + c₁ b
    step (mix (gap b) y) + rot (if b then 7 else 2) x + c₂ b
  let run := fun (ask : Fin d → ℕ → D) (x : W) =>
    (List.finRange d).foldl (fun h j =>
      2 * h + (if ask j h x = 0 then 0 else 1)) (0 : ℕ)
  ∃ (ask : Fin d → ℕ → D) (readout : ℕ → Bool → Fin k → W → F),
    (∀ h b i, cubic (readout h b i)) ∧
    ∀ x b i, (if b then (mark i).2 else (mark i).1) = true →
      out x b i = readout (run ask x) b i x
∀ (k : ℕ) (hk : 0 < k), 7 ≤ k →
  ∀ (mark : Fin k → Bool × Bool) (d : ℕ) (name c₁ c₂ : Bool → Fin k → ZMod 2),
  let ix := fun n : ℕ => (⟨n % k, Nat.mod_lt _ hk⟩ : Fin k)
  let on := fun (b : Bool) (i : Fin k) => if b then (mark i).2 else (mark i).1
  let bag := fun (b : Bool) (i : Fin k) =>
    (Finset.range (if b then 11 else 7)).image (fun r =>
      ix (i.val + k - (if b then 5 else 1) % k + r))
  (∀ (b c : Bool) (i j : Fin k), on b i = true → on c j = true →
    (b,i) ≠ (c,j) → Disjoint (bag b i) (bag c j)) →
  (fits k hk mark d name c₁ c₂ ↔
    ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin k)).filter (fun i => (mark i).1 = true)).card +
      2 * ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin k)).filter (fun i => (mark i).2 = true)).card ≤ d)
changed.unlocks: Price disjoint sparse row and column markings exactly and supply lower bounds for denser markings by taking a disjoint subcollection.

changed.title: Involutions index the full Boolean functions of optimal fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT circuits for the adjacent-width crown
changed.statement:
∀ (k : Nat), 7 ≤ k →
  let A := fun (i : Fin (k+2)) (j : Fin (k+1)) =>
    decide (i.val ≠ k+1 ∧ ¬ (i.val < k ∧ i.val = j.val))
  let Ext := { f : (Fin (k+2) → Bool) → (Fin (k+1) → Bool) → Bool //
    ∃ C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit, PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.FanInTwo C ∧ PEqualNP.Represents.Represents A C ∧ C.size ≤ 2*k+1 ∧
      ∀ x y, f x y = C.eval (List.ofFn x ++ List.ofFn y) }
  let Inv := { perm : Equiv.Perm (Fin k) // Function.Involutive perm }
  ∃ bij : Inv ≃ Ext, ∀ (p : Inv) x y,
    (bij p).val x y = !(x (Fin.last (k+1)) || decide (∃ i : Fin k,
        (x (i.castSucc.castSucc) = true ∧ y (i.castSucc) = true) ∨
        (p.val i ≠ i ∧ ((x (i.castSucc.castSucc) = true ∧ x ((p.val i).castSucc.castSucc) = true) ∨
          (y (i.castSucc) = true ∧ y ((p.val i).castSucc) = true)))))
changed.unlocks: Enumerates all optimal off-promise Boolean behaviors of the adjacent-width family by an explicit bijection.
changed.context: The optimal tree omits the full row and the added column, with the NOT last. Its positive input accepts the empty-row singleton, hence is the OR of this bit with its restriction at zero. Simplifying that restriction leaves a positive tree on 2k ordinary leaves, computing equality on one-hot pairs. Use the involution classification. Conversely add the empty-row OR and the terminal NOT to each such tree. A pair of ordinary row bits with all other bits off distinguishes different transpositions.
